opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grants: £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Long-Term Research); £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications); £2,500 (Research and Travel)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating for at least 12 months) for most categories; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category. Not open to individuals wishing to develop their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions); Acquisitions and Collections; Conferences, Lectures and Publications; Long-Term Research; and Research and Travel grants for individuals. Applications considered four times per year.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture. Fellowships at Studios & Gardens are restricted to projects related to Henry Moore. Artist fellowships are for research only (no studio facilities).
opportunities.summary: Month-long research fellowships enabling artists and researchers to use the Henry Moore Institute's facilities in Leeds (Research Library, Archive of Sculptors' Papers, Leeds Sculpture Collections) or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire. Includes Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships and Senior Fellowships (six weeks). Applications for 2026/27 are closed; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 cash prize for MA dissertation, plus £50 of Institute publications

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines who submitted a dissertation within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertation must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, open to BA and MA students. Winners also receive Henry Moore Institute publications, their dissertations added to the Research Library, and publication of abstracts. The 2025 prize closed; submissions for the 2026 prize open in autumn.
